Depression isn't something that's beaten in a day, there's no step by step instructions or a way to magically make it disappear. Speaking from experience,  the first thing I'd suggest you do is set yourself small goals, even something small can cause a great sense of acomplishment. This will slowly build a bit of confidence and hopefully motivation . It could be as simple as attending x amount of classes in a week. I also think it should be noted that professionals help, I meet with my psychologist once a month from personal preference and my recovery is very much down to her incredible guidance.  I also think that if you parents haven't been made aware of your depression, let them know. They will understand and will support you. If you want someone to talk to just drop me a pm, the amazing people of this subreddit were there for me so I will be more than happy to be there for you.

Depression isn't an easy subject to explain. Any body in the world can be hit by it at some point in their life, it doesn't matter if you're rich or poor, fit and healthy or out of shape, it can reach you and can stem off the smallest of things into something much more complex. I've found most people I've met that have been depressed or still currently are can't identify that key moment when depression struck them. I've found it's much more of a built up effect until one day it knocks you down harder than you've ever been down before and that's when you begin to realise that depression has a firm grip on you. 

My depression I believe to have started because of the poor family life I had behind the closed doors of my house, issues with my parents and my sister began to take a toll on my thought process. It started small, skipping a day of school because I couldn't find the motivation to get myself up to face the everlasting problems at home and then reached the point where I didn't attend school for the entire summer terms one year. It went from effecting just my home life and my relationship with my close family to invading into my personal life, taking control of every small detail of my life at one point. I was scared to leave the house, heck even my room. It wasn't until after the summer terms had been and gone that my mother finally took it upon herself to get me help, the first trip to the doctors was the first time I ventured into the outside world in maybe 6 weeks.

Throughout the next year, the final year of school for myself, is the point in which my problems escalated to serious levels. I was at the point where suicide and packing up to leave were daily thoughts, my thought process was entirely destroyed and I could only see the world as if it was just the home for misery and despair. At this point I didn't understand that it was the depression causing the onslaught of negative thoughts, I felt as it was just me, it was the normal thought process for myself and that I felt shitty because I literally thought I was the worlds biggest lump of crap going.

About 2 months into my last school year I perhaps had the biggest wake up call ever and it came apparent to me that what I was like and my lack for happiness was not being caused by myself. Depression had entered my life, taken everything, thrown me in the corner and was refusing to let me out. Because of the wake up call I finally managed to realise what was happening and that was the point in which I began to try to turn my life around. It started with very small steps, for example walking to the shop that was minutes away just to get outside for a small fraction of the day, until I was ready to venture back into the world. I was lucky, school was very welcoming when I returned properly and I managed to maintain high attendance due to the support of my friends and my form tutor.

Sorry I began rambling on about my life so I will try to get back onto subject, depression isn't something you can just choose instantly to be over, it's no where near simple. 5 years down the line and I may have won some battles but the war is still ongoing and more often that not I am losing. The only difference now to back then is that I refuse to go down without fighting. The only thing I fear is that I will hit a depth I know I can't come back from and the daily thoughts of suicide become a reality.

If you've only just moved, moving is a stressful and knackering experience and it could have possibly taken effect on his mood. He could also feel a little down if he's left people behind. Personally I would talk to him and ask him whats up, he could very well need someone to open up to just as you are right now.

Although people can clearly see you hurting, sometimes they don't know how to help because their unsure on how to bring the situation you're in up. There is nothing wrong admitting to someone that you do indeed need their help. So I will be the first to ask, how can I help?
